Lessons.Title: Compose and Decompose to Add and Subtract
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will review how to add and subtract multi-digit numbers with composition and decomposition.
In earlier grades, you encountered subtraction problems which required decomposing a unit. In this lesson, you review this idea of decomposition and revisit how it is recorded when using the standard algorithm to subtract numbers through the thousands place. You also use composition to add multi-digit numbers through the hundred-thousands place. - Representation
Core relationship: Compose and decompose within the standard algorithms. Regroup a place into ten of the next smaller place without changing number value.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Number Talk: Subtract Fractions	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Find and Check Sums	 (15 minutes); Activity 2:  Priya’s Family Heirlooms	 (20 minutes); Cool-down:  Difference and then Sum	 (5 minutes)
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): Subtract 18,597 from 91,000.
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Borrowing from a zero without regrouping across the next nonzero place.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Regroup a place into ten of the next smaller place without changing number value.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Subtracting eight ones from four without exchanging a ten.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The mathematical operation or unit interpretation is incorrect.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Exchange a ten for ten ones before subtracting.
